hypothesis: The validated P70_L40d strategy, when stress-tested via 10,000 Monte Carlo simulations of bootstrapped trade outcomes, demonstrates acceptable risk-adjusted returns and drawdown characteristics for paper trading consideration.
method: Bootstrap resampling of 1,522 individual trade P&Ls from validated P70_L40d strategy (2023-2025). Each simulation draws 507 trades with replacement (1 year equivalent). 10,000 simulations. Note: individual trade P&Ls resampled — financial time series NOT shuffled.

CAVEAT-1.title: 95th percentile max drawdown is 75.6% — severe
CAVEAT-1.detail: In 5% of simulations the strategy loses 75.6%+ of capital before recovering. On ₹20,000, that means hitting ₹4,880 before recovering. Psychologically and practically this is very hard to survive. A trader at ₹20k who sees ₹15,000 disappear will almost certainly exit before the strategy recovers.
CAVEAT-1.implication: Minimum recommended capital for psychological and practical survival: ₹50,000–1,00,000. At ₹50k a 75% drawdown leaves ₹12,500 — still enough to maintain 1-lot positions.

CAVEAT-2.title: 30% win rate means long losing streaks are mathematically expected
CAVEAT-2.detail: With 30% win rate, the probability of 8 consecutive losses = 0.7^8 = 5.8%. In 507 trades/year, you will likely experience multiple 6-9 loss streaks. In live trading, this psychological pressure causes most traders to abandon a valid strategy.
CAVEAT-2.implication: Paper trading for 3+ months required to build confidence in the loss streaks before deploying real capital.

CAVEAT-3.title: Returns are inflated by flat 14% IV assumption — real IV varies 10-35%
CAVEAT-3.detail: The options pricer uses 14% flat IV throughout. Real market IV on NIFTY weekly options varies from 10% (quiet markets) to 35%+ (crisis days). When you buy options in high-IV environments, you overpay for premium and the subsequent IV crush reduces your profits significantly. This single assumption likely inflates returns by 20-40%.
CAVEAT-3.implication: Real live returns will be lower than MC suggests. Treat headline returns with caution. Priority for next research phase: replace flat IV with real market IV data.

CAVEAT-4.title: Returns are driven by a few large winning trades (right-skewed distribution)
CAVEAT-4.detail: Avg win ₹2,198, avg loss ₹498 (4.41x ratio). This means a small number of large winners drive the strategy's profitability. In a bootstrap, these large winners recur at their historical frequency. But in live trading, wide bid-ask spreads on NIFTY options can easily reduce a ₹2,198 winner to ₹1,500 while the ₹498 loser stays at ₹498 — significantly compressing the win/loss ratio.
CAVEAT-4.implication: Slippage and execution costs will impact large winning trades more than small losing trades. Real profit factor is likely 1.3-1.5 not 1.89.

CAVEAT-5.title: Bootstrap samples from 3 years; if 2026+ market regime changes, results change
CAVEAT-5.detail: All 1,522 trades come from 2023-2025. If future market conditions are systematically different (structural ATR change, SEBI regulation change on weekly options), the trade distribution will be different from what we sampled.
CAVEAT-5.implication: The adaptive ATR filter partially addresses this (adapts to current volatility) but does not protect against structural regime shifts.

minimum_capital_recommendation.rationale: 95th pctile max drawdown of 75.6% on ₹20k = account drops to ₹4,880. On ₹50k = drops to ₹12,200 (still enough for 2-3 lots). On ₹1L = drops to ₹24,400 (still 5+ lots). Minimum capital should allow the strategy to survive its worst-case drawdown and still trade.

realistic_return_estimate.rationale: After accounting for real IV (not flat 14%), bid-ask spread on options (~₹2-5/unit = ₹100-250/lot), slippage on high-vol days, and psychological factors reducing trade count, realistic returns are a fraction of the backtest median. 200% annual return would still be extraordinary.

conclusion: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED — Monte Carlo gate PASSED on all 3 criteria. Sharpe 3.00, ruin probability 17.8% (<20%), annual loss probability 1.6% (<35%). The strategy shows strong statistical characteristics. HOWEVER: the 95th percentile drawdown (75.6%) and 30% win rate demand respect. The headline return of 777% median will compress significantly in live trading due to IV assumptions, slippage, and bid-ask spread on options. A realistic expectation is 150-400% annually at ₹50k capital with careful execution. The next gate is PAPER TRADING: 3 months of live signals (not deployed yet) to validate that the backtest signal logic matches real market microstructure.
next_gate: PAPER_TRADING — wire the validated strategy to live data feed, generate signals, track paper P&L for minimum 3 months before real capital deployment
